business_problem: VIVOTEK needed to launch a secure, scalable cloud surveillance platform quickly without spending time building custom camera-to-cloud infrastructure or diverting engineering effort away from new AI-powered features.
solution_summary: VIVOTEK launched its VORTEX video-surveillance-as-a-service platform on AWS to avoid building bespoke camera-to-cloud infrastructure and to speed delivery of a global, scalable surveillance offering. Security cameras connect through AWS IoT Core, which handles cloud onboarding and messaging from field devices. Application workloads then run on Amazon EC2 and Amazon EKS, while Amazon RDS and Amazon DynamoDB persist platform data and Amazon S3 stores cloud content. Amazon SNS supports notifications across the service. This multi-tier architecture let VIVOTEK bring full-stack web and mobile applications to market in 12 months while offloading infrastructure complexity to managed AWS services. With operations simplified, engineering could focus most of its effort on innovation and on advancing the AI-powered capabilities of the VORTEX surveillance platform.

solution_components.name: AWS IoT Core
solution_components.role: Connects security cameras to the cloud and removes the need for VIVOTEK to build its own camera-connection layer.

solution_components.name: Amazon EC2
solution_components.role: Provides compute capacity for VORTEX application workloads.

solution_components.name: Amazon EKS
solution_components.role: Runs containerized parts of the surveillance platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon RDS
solution_components.role: Stores relational platform data for the VORTEX service.

solution_components.name: Amazon DynamoDB
solution_components.role: Stores scalable application data for the surveillance platform.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Stores cloud content associated with the surveillance solution.

solution_components.name: Amazon SNS
solution_components.role: Handles notifications across the VORTEX service.
